newsitem.title: NIGERIA: African leaders delay Liberia poll till July 19.
newsitem.headline: African leaders delay Liberia poll till July 19.

text.p: West African heads of state have postponed Liberia's post-war general elections to July 19 instead of May 30.

"They approved that the election day will be Saturday 19th of July 1997 with the inauguration of the new government on 2nd of August, 1997," said an official communiqu after Wednesday's one-day summit of the committee of nine, an Economic Community of West African States group overseeing Liberia's peace agreement.
The communique said in the event of a run-off, this would be conducted on August 2 and the new government inaugurated on August 16th.

The 16-nation ECOWAS brokered the end of Liberia's seven year civil war last year and the presidential and legislative vote will consolidate the peace enforced by a Nigerian-led West African peace-keeping force called ECOMOG.

Liberian leaders, including former warlords now presidential candidates, had called for a postponement of the vote until August or September for security reasons, logistics and lack of voter education.
"We hope that this meeting will be the last to be held for the resolution of the Liberian crisis," Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha told the closing session of the Abuja summit.
